Test whether two context trees differ, with a permutation test

Source: R/compare.R
compare_trees.Rd

compare_trees() tests whether two fitted context trees, one per group, predict differently overall, with a permutation test. The test statistic is the count-weighted symmetric Kullback-Leibler divergence between the trees' next-state distributions, the quantity returned by tree_distance(); two groups of sequences can pass through the same states and still differ in what tends to follow a given history.

The divergence has no known sampling distribution and is positive even when both groups come from one process, so the reference distribution is built by permutation. The sequences of the two trees are pooled, reassigned at random to two groups of the original sizes, and two trees are refitted with each original tree's depth, minimum count, smoothing and pruning; this is repeated iter times. The p-value is the share of permuted distances at least as large as the observed one, counting the observed value once (\((1 + b) / (iter + 1)\)). A per-context table shows which histories contribute most to the distance. The result is a transitiontrees_comparison object, read with as.data.frame() and summary() and drawn with plot().

The comparison is pairwise and treats sequences as exchangeable. For more than two groups, for separate tests of what follows a context and how often it is reached, for per-context p-values with false discovery rate control, or for a permutation stratified by person when one person contributes several sequences, use compare_groups().

Usage

compare_trees(tree_a, tree_b = NULL, iter = 200L, seed = 1L, symmetric = TRUE)

Arguments

tree_a, tree_b

Unweighted transitiontrees objects fitted to the two groups. Alternatively a transitiontrees_group with two groups as tree_a and tree_b = NULL (default); its two trees are compared in group order.

iter

Number of permutations. Default 200.

seed

Seed for the permutations. Default 1. The call sets the session's random-number state.

symmetric

TRUE (default) for the symmetric divergence; FALSE for \(D_{KL}(A \| B)\) alone.

Value

An object of class transitiontrees_comparison. Its tables are returned by as.data.frame(x, what = "pathways") (one row per context in either tree: counts in each tree and the two directed and the symmetric divergence) and as.data.frame(x, what = "null") (one row per permutation); summary() gives one row with the observed distance, the null mean, standard deviation and 95th percentile, and the p-value; plot() draws the null distribution.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input

(error) an argument is not a transitiontrees object; tree_b missing; a transitiontrees_group without exactly two groups, or given together with tree_b; iter not a positive number.

transitiontrees_weighted_unsupported

(error) a tree was fitted with weights; the permutation refits from the raw sequences and would drop them.

transitiontrees_alphabet_mismatch

(error) the trees have different alphabets.

See also

summary.transitiontrees_comparison, as.data.frame.transitiontrees_comparison and plot.transitiontrees_comparison for the result; tree_distance() for the distance alone; compare_groups() for several groups and per-context tests.

Examples

grp <- context_tree(group_regulation_long, actor = "Actor", time = "Time",
                    action = "Action", group = "Achiever", max_depth = 1)
cmp <- compare_trees(grp, iter = 20)
cmp
#> <transitiontrees_comparison>  iter = 20
#>   observed distance : 0.0471
#>   null mean         : 0.00294
#>   p-value           : 0.0476
#> 
#> top divergent pathways:
#>     pathway count_a count_b divergence_ab divergence_ba divergence_sym
#>   synthesis     278     374         0.300         0.311          0.305
#>     discuss    2003    1948         0.178         0.204          0.191
#>    cohesion     938     757         0.120         0.115          0.117
#>       adapt     141     368         0.044         0.094          0.069
#>   consensus    3392    2937         0.050         0.046          0.048
#>  coregulate     894    1076         0.046         0.047          0.046
summary(cmp)
#> <transitiontrees_comparison summary>
#>  distance null_mean  null_sd null_q95 p_value iter n_pathways
#>    0.0471   0.00294 0.000556  0.00378  0.0476   20         10
